messages:
support-bot: Alert from Support — customer Sandbird reports a ~40% throughput drop on dedicated pool A (started ~08:10 UTC). p90 latency up from 120ms -> 400ms. filing here for investigation.

mike: thanks. is this after the model variant rollout this morning?

support-bot: yes, rollout redwood-7b-q4r2 -> redwood-7b-q4r3 at 07:58 UTC. No config changes reported by customer.

anya: assigning myself to run a quick synthetic. can someone drop the exact endpoint + headers?

kevin: endpoint is https://dedicated-us-west.api.redwood/v1/generate (sandbird-prod key). use header `x-customer: sandbird-prod` and `X-Model: redwood-7b-q4r3`.

anya: running wrk now: `wrk -t8 -c150 -d30s --latency --timeout 10s "https://dedicated-us-west.api.redwood/v1/generate?model=redwood-7b-q4r3"`

mike: also: please capture KV cache hit metrics and probe kernel selector logs on the host (`/var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log`) while you run.

anya: done. preliminary numbers: 35% lower throughput vs baseline. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.82 -> 0.44 on this load. attaching tail of logs: `KVCache: prefix_miss=1623 prefix_hit=1135 total=2758`

ryan: that suggests cache key mismatch — maybe variant changed serialization or shard key. kevin any recent kernel/serialization changes in that rollout?

kevin: PR #3421 changed the kv-key packing for attention cache to include a `model_variant` byte to avoid collisions across variants. Might be we're mismatching for existing warm caches. if servers still have old cache entries serialized without the byte, new variant won't hit.

lorna: if that's the case, customers with warm KV would see regression immediately after variant flip. can we confirm deploy strategy for the rollout? deploy-bot: rolling update -> hosts replaced in-place, no cache flush.

mike: ok action items: 1) anya to re-run synthetic on previous variant (q4r2) for baseline; 2) kevin to triage PR #3421 and produce quick revert or compatibility shim; 3) ryan to draft rollback runbook for dedicated pool; 4) lorna to coordinate customer comms and optional call.

anya: baseline run (q4r2) now: throughput matches previous numbers. KV hit 0.81. so regression reproduces locally.

kevin: hopping into the PR now. quick theory: new packing adds leading byte, so old entries won't match. two quick fixes: a) revert the change (fast) or b) accept both serializations in lookup (compat shim) — I'll prototype (b) to avoid extra rollout churn.

mike: prefer shim if low-risk. if prototype >10m, revert and we can re-release with shim.

kevin: prototype done in a branch, added fallback lookup path: try keyed lookup with new byte, if miss try legacy lookup. small perf penalty on a miss path, but should restore hit-rates. bench locally: restored throughput to baseline under same wrk load.

mike: nice. can you cut a hotfix PR and tag @anya for a quick canary deploy on 2 hosts?

kevin: PR #3498 created, CI green. req reviewers: mike, anya.

anya: will canary on two hosts in us-west dedicated pool. will run 2x 30s wrk and post metrics.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: hosts host-0345, host-0412 receiving image redwood-runtime:hotfix-3498.

anya: canary results: p99/p50/p90 back to baseline. KV hit restored to ~0.8. customer sandbox looks stable.

mike: thanks. next steps: (a) roll hotfix across pool with 10% batch, (b) notify Sandbird support that we identified kv serialization mismatch introduced by variant byte and we deployed a compatibility shim, (c) open retro for better rollout checklist around cache serialization.

lorna: scheduling customer sync in 30m to confirm impact and ask if they'd like us to flush caches or keep shim. pinging Sandbird PM. :phone: 

ryan: I'll prepare rollback runbook in case canary shows issues during roll.

mike: final ask — kevin: please include a short note in PR describing the change and potential long-term plan (e.g., versioned cache schema + migration) so eng-sre can bake it into rollout playbook.

kevin: will do. thanks all — marking as resolved in thread once full roll completes.

support-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026 updated: mitigation deployed (hotfix-3498), rolling across pool. customer notified.

mike: :thumbsup: great work.
